title: rk unified projection graph document (v1)
description: Read-only, deterministic, stateless projection of one rk research campaign (PRD C5, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md M2.1). The registry (argument/**/*.md shards) is the spine (`nodes`); the other three stores — af, bd, fr — and the generated report join to it by DIFFERENT keys per edge (`edges.af` / `edges.bd` / `edges.fr` / `edges.report`) — there is no universal join key, do not invent one. `unresolved` is a first-class bucket every edge kind's failed lookups land in (never a silent drop). `conflicts` is a first-class defect record (registry-vs-af disagreement, contract mismatch, taint-vs-status inconsistency, fr banked-without-oracle); M2.3 populates it, this schema only reserves the shape. See docs/memos/2026-07-19-graph-schema-v1.md for the design rationale and src/graph/{types,serialize,validate}.ts for the TS mirror + canonical serializer + structural validator (this JSON Schema alone cannot express referential integrity, unresolved-bucket completeness, or canonical sort order — those are src/graph/validate.ts's job).

schema_version.description: Consumers must check this before parsing the rest of the document; a version bump accompanies any incompatible shape change (CLAUDE.md rule 10), with a fixture. Mirrors the convention set by ../vibefeld's `af export --graph json` (docs/export-graph-v1.md).

nodes.description: The registry spine, one entry per argument/**/*.md shard. MUST be sorted by `id` ascending in the canonical form (src/graph/serialize.ts) — this is part of the document's identity, not a rendering nicety.

edges.description: The four per-edge joins (PRD C5 table). Each array's canonical sort order is defined in src/graph/serialize.ts, not here.

af.description: registry↔af: contract byte-match, LOCATED VIA the shard's `workspace:` field (never the registry id — workspace directories can be renamed independently of the registry id; see ../vibefeld/docs/export-graph-v1.md's `workspace.id` note). Known hazard: workspace dir ≠ id after a rename (legal) — keyed on `workspace:`, always.

bd.description: registry↔bd: registry id IS the bd issue key (linker-synced issues). No known hazard.

fr.description: registry↔fr: `evidence.artifact` path resolution + `graduates`/oracle ids. Known hazard: free-text paths — expect a real unresolved-reference bucket, never silently dropped.

report.description: registry↔report: shard label/id anchors (as check-provenance.py's own anchor resolution does today). Known hazard: anchors are ids, not contracts.

unresolved.description: The first-class unresolved-reference bucket (PRD C5): every edge kind's failed lookups land here, `(edge, ref)`-keyed. A consumer must be able to answer "what did rk try to join and fail" from this array alone, without re-deriving it from the edge arrays' `resolved` flags.

conflicts.description: First-class defect records — registry-status vs af-epistemic-state disagreement, contract byte-mismatch, taint vs status inconsistency, fr banked-claim without oracle verdict. M2.3 populates these; this schema (M2.1) only reserves the shape. Conflicts are rendered, never auto-resolved.

balloonCounter.description: Reserved (PRD C9 / M3.6 balloon feedback loop): present and zero-valued from M2.1 on, populated only once M3.6 lands.

path.description: repo-relative path to this shard's own file. Never a join key itself — `id` and `workspace` are.

workspace.description: THE join key into af. Raw `workspace:` frontmatter value, e.g. "proofs/lem-x". Absent iff the shard never declared one. NEVER assumed equal to `id` — see edges.af's description and the rename-hazard note above.

deps.description: AND-edges: registry ids. Semantically a SET — canonical order is sorted, not insertion order.

routes.description: OR-groups: each inner array is one route (AND); the outer array is the disjunction (any one route suffices). `[]` when the shard declares no routes.

defs.description: Layer-0 definitions/*.md ids this node cites.

workspace.description: Copied from the owning node's own `workspace:` field — MUST be byte-identical to it (src/graph/validate.ts enforces this cross-check; a drift means a producer re-derived the join key from `id` instead of copying the field, the exact rename-hazard bug class).

resolved.description: true iff an af export was found for `workspace` AND its contract byte-matched some node's `statement` in that export. false MUST carry a companion entry in the top-level `unresolved` array (edge:"af", ref:workspace).

afNodeId.description: Which af node's `statement` matched, when resolved (usually "1", the root).

contractMatch.description: Explicit byte-match verdict, independent of `resolved`: a workspace can resolve (an export was found) while its statement no longer matches — that is a CONFLICT (M2.3), not an unresolved reference.

afSchemaVersion.description: The af export document's own schema_version (../vibefeld/docs/export-graph-v1.md), echoed for traceability — NOT this document's schema_version.

frEdge.description: Keyed by fr's own `cycle` (fr's log.jsonl identity), NOT by registry id — one fr cycle resolves to zero or one registry node.

artifact.description: The free-text `evidence.artifact` value from fr's LogRecord — the known hazard (free-text paths).

anchor.description: The report label/id anchor — an id, not a contract.

ref.description: The raw reference text that failed to resolve — a workspace path (af), a registry id (bd), a free-text artifact string (fr), or an anchor (report).

nodeId.description: The registry node this unresolved lookup was attempted FROM, when known.

sourceCycle.description: fr's own cycle number, when edge=="fr".

kind.description: Open vocabulary — M2.1 reserves the shape only. Known values as of M2.1 (populated starting M2.3): "status-mismatch", "contract-mismatch", "taint-status-mismatch", "banked-without-oracle".
